s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic ankle pain and swelling with bony lesion
salient_findings: Pain and swelling around the right ankle for 1 year
Bony thickening over the lateral malleolus
Submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin
key_facts: 13-year-old boy
1-year history of pain and swelling around the right ankle
Gradually increasing in size
Bony thickening over the lateral malleolus
Ankle and subtalar joints have a full range of motion
Complete blood count within normal limits
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 68 mm at the first hour
Submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin
Plain radiography of the right ankle revealed a lytic lesion

shortlist.label: Brodie’s abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Submetaphyseal lytic lesion with a well-defined sclerotic margin and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Osteoid osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bony thickening and pain around the ankle, consistent with a benign bone tumor

shortlist.label: Osteoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin, similar to osteoblastoma presentation

shortlist.label: Chondroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion with a well-defined sclerotic margin, and the patient's age is consistent with chondroblastoma

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion in the epiphysis or metaphysis, and the patient's age is consistent with giant cell tumor

raw.rationale: The presence of a submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin, along with elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and a long history of pain and swelling, is consistent with the diagnosis of Brodie’s abscess, a type of chronic osteomyelitis.

rejected.label: Osteoid osteoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with severe nocturnal pain that is relieved by NSAIDs, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Osteoblastoma
rejected.why: Usually presents with more aggressive features and a larger size than the lesion described

rejected.label: Chondroblastoma
rejected.why: Typically occurs in the epiphysis and has a distinct radiographic appearance with a 'chicken wire' calcification pattern, not mentioned here

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Usually occurs after skeletal maturity and has a more aggressive radiographic appearance with 'soap bubble' lesions
